class_name: 否定-不可能-ワケニハイカナイ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Denies permissibility rather than ability: the act is perfectly doable, but duty, conscience or circumstances rule it out (運転前に飲むわけにはいかない), which is what separates it from 〜ことができない. Attached to a negated verb it flips into obligation (行かないわけにはいかない, "I have no choice but to go"). It typically describes a human predicament the speaker is inside of; わけにゃ is the spoken contraction of わけには.

examples.ruby: 一口[ひとくち]だけと言[い]われても、運転[うんてん]前[まえ]に飲[の]むわけにはいかない。
examples.english: They said just one sip, but I can't very well drink before driving.

examples.ruby: 借[か]りた本[ほん]を汚[よご]したまま返[かえ]すわけにはいかない。
examples.english: I can't very well hand a borrowed book back with a stain still on it.

examples.ruby: ここまで来[き]て、今[いま]さらやめるわけにゃいかない。
examples.english: We've come this far; no way we're quitting now.

patterns.usage_note: Rules an act out as impermissible, with the conjectural まい offering the refusal as a judgment the hearer is expected to share rather than a flat assertion (見捨てるわけにはいくまい). It belongs to written narration and deliberative monologue; ordinary conversation says わけにはいかないだろう. まい already carries the negation, so いく takes no further negative, while the preceding verb freely does: 〜ないわけにはいくまい is the obligation shape.

examples.ruby: これほど世話[せわ]になった相手[あいて]を見捨[みす]てるわけにはいくまい。
examples.english: After all he has done for us, we can hardly abandon him.

examples.ruby: 部下[ぶか]の失態[しったい]なのだから、知[し]らぬ顔[かお]をするわけにはいくまい。
examples.english: It was my subordinate's blunder; I can scarcely pretend not to notice.

examples.ruby: 事[こと]ここに至[いた]っては、真相[しんそう]を伏[ふ]せておくわけにはいくまい。
examples.english: Matters having come to this, it would hardly do to keep the truth hidden.

patterns.usage_note: Negative resolve in the first person: the speaker rules an act out for himself (二度と入るまい, 誰にも相談するまい), the negative twin of the volitional よう. The sibling lane is negative conjecture about an event or another person (雨は降るまい, 失敗するまい); here the subject is the speaker, often with a framing verb of decision (〜まいと決めた, 〜まいと誓う). Everyday speech now prefers ないつもりだ.

examples.ruby: あんな店[みせ]には二度[にど]と入[はい]るまいと心[こころ]に決[き]めた。
examples.english: I made up my mind never to set foot in that shop again.

examples.ruby: もう約束[やくそく]の時間[じかん]に遅[おく]れるまいと、早[はや]めに家[いえ]を出[で]た。
examples.english: Determined never to be late for an appointment again, I left the house early.

examples.ruby: この件[けん]については、誰[だれ]にも相談[そうだん]するまい。
examples.english: On this matter I won't be consulting anyone.
